newsitem.title: FRANCE: French non-communist left to win absolute majority.
newsitem.headline: French non-communist left to win absolute majority.

text.p: France's Socialist party and allies looked set to win an absolute majority in France's parliamentary election on Sunday, television projections showed.
This would mean a Socialist-led government would not have to depend on the Communist Party for support.

The Sofres polling institute showed the Socialist party and allies winning 289 seats, the number of seats required for an absolute majority, compared to 235 for the ruling RPR/UDF coalition, 36 for the Communist Party, one for the extreme-right National Front.
The BVA polling institute gave the Socialists and their allies 290 seats, compared to 230 for the RPR/UDF coalition, 36 for the Communist Party, one for the National Front.
The CSA polling institute gave the Socialist party and allies 290 seats, compared to 225 for the RPR/UDF, 35 for the Communist Party, two for the National Front.
